question: Does original client data identify Repair-O-Matic ammo, and does it establish the Alia Das vendor's template-56 stock or three-credit price?
result: The compatible original client directly maps Repair-O-Matic reward template 122871 to weapon class 12797; that class uses ammo class 3807 and a 10-round clip. Client template 56 maps to class 3807, whose English display name is Standard Grade Power Cells. These are original client-side identities for this compatible build. No inspected original client table specifies creature 73's stock or template 56's sale price. The Alia Das stock and three-credit price remain current emulator data, not verified final-live values.
client_build_scope: 1.16.5.0 is the emulator compatibility build, not independently proven to be the exact shutdown build. Static client definitions cannot establish final-live server inventory, price or mission reward grants.

client_package.method: Read ZIP members and disassemble Python 2.4 code objects with xdis; offsets below are bytecode instruction offsets inside the named module, not ZIP byte positions.

original_client_rows.finding: Repair-O-Matic reward template uses weapon class 12797.

original_client_rows.locator: lookup assignment at bytecode 55075-55160: key 12797, tuple fields include ammo class 3807 at 55096 and clip size 10 at 55099
original_client_rows.finding: Weapon class 12797 consumes ammo class 3807 and holds 10 rounds.
Item template 56 represents ammo class 3807 in this client.

original_client_rows.locator: entityclass bytecode 8614-8620: class 3807 -> Ammo_Battery_1_Standard_Grade; English physicalentityclassnamelanguage bytecode 2749-2756: 3807 -> Standard Grade Power Cells
original_client_rows.finding: The ammo class has the client display name Standard Grade Power Cells.

original_client_rows.tier: original, limited to vendor package presentation category
original_client_rows.locator: vendorpackages assignment at bytecode 862-869: package 104 -> (2, None, 1); module constant 2 is GENERAL_GOODS
original_client_rows.finding: Client package 104 has a General Goods presentation category. The module does not enumerate package stock or item prices. The current emulator associates creature 73 with package 104, but that association is server data.

contemporary_play_evidence.tier: observed firsthand account, older than final live
contemporary_play_evidence.source: Michael Zenke, Adventures From the Back Row: the Specialist and her tools, 2007-11-26, https://www.engadget.com/2007-11-26-adventures-from-the-back-row-the-specialist-and-her-tools.html
contemporary_play_evidence.exact_location: Paragraph beginning 'The repair tool operates in much the same way'
contemporary_play_evidence.finding: Repair tools consume Power Cells when used on a target with damaged armor.
contemporary_play_evidence.limit: This confirms the ammo type in 2007 play, but names no Alia Das vendor, template ID, stock, price or final-live mission 2011 ammo grant.

emulator_vendor_provenance.tier: emulator seed, unverified against final-live source
emulator_vendor_provenance.source_history: git commit 5fabca7 dated 2023-02-20 introduced vendor 73 -> 56 in a 'Draft ... re-populated vendors' change; the same commit message does not identify an original retail capture. ItemTemplatePreloader template 56 row blames to commit 564d4e3 dated 2023-02-14, which describes adding vendors 'as per the map'. This history does not establish retail stock or price.
emulator_vendor_provenance.finding: The current three-credit Alia Das sale is an emulator behavior. Its final-live accuracy remains unverified.

decision: Treat template 56 as the original compatible-client identity for Standard Grade Power Cells and a plausible ordinary ammo source if actually stocked. Do not label Alia Das creature 73's template-56 stock or three-credit price original or observed final-live; keep both as evidence gaps. Do not add a class-gear ammo grant from this evidence.
